title: Lines in the prime number graph
summary: The prime number graph is the set of points $(n,p_n)$ where $p_n$ denotes the $n^{\rm th}$ prime. Let $L(n)$ be the minimum number of straight line segments needed to cover the first $n$ points in this set. Let $B(n)$ be the largest number of points $(k,p_k)$ with $k\le n$ covered by a single line. Recently Sloane conjectured that $L(n) = O(n/\log n)$. We show that $L(n)=O(n \log \log n / \log n)$ and $B(n)\ge c\log n$ for a constant $c>0$ and all large $n$.
